overview.narrative:
REIT performance was mixed on July 15, with Hospitality leading at +1.00% on average as summer travel demand continues to support hotel fundamentals—HST paced the group at +1.80%. Office surprised to the upside at +0.77%, led by SLG's +1.84% move, likely reflecting renewed return-to-office momentum in gateway markets. Housing was the clear laggard at -0.60%, with apartment names ESS (-1.79%) and MAA (-1.43%) under pressure alongside ELME (-1.95%), suggesting investors are pricing in softer rental growth as new supply deliveries weigh on Sunbelt and coastal markets alike.

The standout divergence is ARE surging +2.53%—the day's top gainer—while broader Healthcare averaged -0.08% and SBRA dropped -1.16%, indicating this is a company-specific life sciences catalyst rather than a sector rotation. Retail and Netlease both flatlined near zero, with O slipping -0.80%, consistent with duration-sensitive names struggling amid a steepening yield curve. LEN's +1.89% gain within the weak Housing cohort underscores the ongoing bifurcation between homebuilders and apartment landlords.

Positioning into tomorrow, we favor leaning into the Hospitality and Office momentum while remaining cautious on multifamily until supply headwinds abate. Watch the long end closely—further curve steepening could keep Netlease and triple-net names under pressure. ARE warrants monitoring for follow-through.
